Story & Plot

Following the death of Shivaji, the Maratha-Mughal conflict sparks across the region as his son Sambhaji leads the resistance against Aurangzeb's forces. Amid battles and political intrigue, both sides face major challenges in a fierce struggle for power. The historical film brings the story of Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj to the screen with intensity and emotion.

Comedy & Entertainment

As a historical action drama centered around a tense struggle for power and fierce battles, the film does not focus on traditional humor. Instead, its entertainment value relies heavily on the historical conflict, emotional intensity, and high-stakes drama between opposing forces. The narrative is driven by tension and valor rather than lighthearted or comical moments.

Performances & Direction

The cast features Vicky Kaushal, Rashmika Mandanna, Akshaye Khanna, Ashutosh Rana, and Divya Dutta under the direction of Laxman Utekar. Reviewers highlight Vicky Kaushal for his outstanding and fierce portrayal of Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj, bringing the historical figure to life with a lot of intensity and emotion. Additionally, Akshaye Khanna is noted as a scene-stealer in his role as Aurangzeb.

Strengths

  • Outstanding portrayal of Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj by Vicky Kaushal
  • Akshaye Khanna as a scene-stealer
  • Brings historical legacy and intensity to the screen
  • Powerful performances and dialogues in key moments
  • Captures themes of courage and valor

Weaknesses

Reviewers note that the storytelling could have been tighter and the filmmaking is hampered by an aimless screenplay, plot inconsistencies, and repetitive dialogue. Some critics found the film paradoxically dull despite extreme violence, arguing that a two to three hour runtime can never do full justice to the history.

Final verdict

Chhaava delivers a powerful historical saga anchored by phenomenal lead performances, particularly from Vicky Kaushal and Akshaye Khanna. While it suffers from an aimless screenplay and storytelling inconsistencies, its emotional intensity and portrayal of courage make it a notable watch for fans of historical dramas. Viewers interested in the Maratha-Mughal conflict will find worthwhile moments in its depiction of valor.
